1 دَعَكَهُ , (S, K,) aor.
دَعَكَ , (K,) inf. n. دَعْكٌ, (S,) He rubbed it, or rubbed and pressed it, (S, * K, TA,) or did so well, (KL,) and softened it; (TA;) namely, a skin, or hide. (S, K, TA.) ―
-b2- He softened its (i. e. a garment's) roughness by wearing it. (K.) ―
-b3- He softened him, (S, K,) and subdued him, or rendered him submissive; (TA;) namely, an adversary, or antagonist; (S, K;) and so مَعَكَهُ, inf. n. مَعْكٌ. (TA.) ―
-b4- دَعَكَهُ فِى التُّرَابِ He rolled him, or turned him over, in the dust. (K.) ―
-b5- دَعَكْتُ الرَّجُلَ بِالقَوْلِ I pained the man by speech. (IDrd.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
